title: feat(types): declare `cardTitle` on `ObjectKanbanSchema` (objectui#9606)
body:
Fixes #9606

Clause-②: yes — a published mirror's accepted set widens to the spec's own set. Contract review at tier; this PR stays **draft** and is deliberately not enqueued and not given auto-merge.

Executing director seat batch #150 item 3, letter 1 (maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-17T15:25Z), with the lane correction to `domain:spec`.

## What changed

Located **by symbol**, and cited that way on purpose — line addresses in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` have drifted before, and this card is itself about a drifted mirror. (Measured drift: the ruling cites the kanban arm at `:2104`; on today's `origin/main` `2923cea165` that address does hold. The ruling also cites the spec pair at `component.zod.ts:2845-2846`, which is the objectstack checkout's current main — in the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` this repo actually resolves, the same pair sits 135 lines earlier.)

- **`ObjectKanbanSchema` in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`** gains `cardTitle`, declared `z.string().optional()`, immediately above the legacy `titleField` — the order the spec declares the pair in.
- **The `ObjectKanbanSchema` interface in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`** gains `cardTitle?: string` beside `titleField?: string`, at the same requiredness.
- **New pin** `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-kanban-card-title-9606.test.ts` — 14 runtime rows plus one compile-time row.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/9606-object-kanban-card-title.md`, `@object-ui/types` **minor**.

⛔ `titleField` is **not** retired and was not touched beyond being left declared. A mirror cannot be narrower than the spec it mirrors, and `@objectstack/spec` still declares the alias.

## The describe string, copied rather than paraphrased

Read from the installed package this repo resolves — `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, `src/ui/component.zod.ts`, and cross-read against that package's shipped `json-schema/ui/ObjectKanbanProps.json`, which carries the same two strings as `description`:

- `cardTitle` — `Field rendered as each card title`
- `titleField` — `` Legacy fallback for `cardTitle` (the board reads `cardTitle || titleField`). Prefer `cardTitle` ``

The mirror's `describe` carries the first string verbatim as its leading clause and then states the pair relationship: `` Field rendered as each card title — the canonical spelling; `titleField` beside it is the legacy fallback, and the board reads `cardTitle || titleField` ``.

## The opposite-answer measurement — the same probe, before and after

`safeValidateSchema({ type: 'object-kanban', objectName: 'tasks', groupBy: 'status', cardTitle: 42 })`, run through vitest on this worktree and written to disk by the probe itself:

| | before (`origin/main` `2923cea165`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | **true** | **false** |
| parsed document | **keeps `cardTitle: 42`** | no document |
| issue reported | none | `cardTitle: Invalid input: expected string, received number` |

Both controls answer the same both times: `cardTitle: 'name'` → accepted, `titleField: 'name'` → accepted. The card's own premise therefore held on measurement, including the part that matters most — the `42` was not merely admitted, it **survived the parse** and reached `resolveKanbanTitleField`, which returns it as a record field name.

Instrument check on the same corpus: `cardTitle` read **0** times in `zod/objectql.zod.ts` before this change, against a lit control of **262** `key: z.…` declarations in that same file, and `titleField` reading on **17** lines. Two of the numbers quoted upstream differ from what this tree reads — the card and triage both say 263 and 10 — and the difference is drift in the file, not a disagreement about the finding.

## Ablation — each pin mutated, proven on disk, restored

**Leg 1 — the zod declaration.** `cardTitle: z.string().optional()` mutated to `cardTitle: z.any().optional()` as a whole expression. Anchor count 1 → 0, injected text 0 → 1, byte delta −3, blob `1c6ce1fe…` → `006f5828…`. Pin run: **exit 1**, `Tests 2 failed | 12 passed (14)` — the two rows that assert the refusal, one through `ObjectKanbanSchema` and one through `safeValidateSchema`. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path: blob back to `1c6ce1fe…` and `git diff HEAD` empty (0 bytes); re-run **exit 0**, `14 passed`.

**Leg 2 — the TypeScript twin.** `cardTitle?: string;` replaced by a comment, verified with literal (`grep -cF`) counts in both directions: anchor 1 → 0, marker 0 → 1, byte delta +24, blob `ad8b656a…` → `e44564b1…`. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` → **exit 2**, `error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.` Restored: blob back to `ad8b656a…`, `git diff HEAD` for that path empty, re-run **exit 0**.

## ⚠️ A premise of the ruling that did NOT survive measurement

The ruling's stated reason for mirroring the TypeScript twin is "so the zod-mirror-parity ratchet stays at zero drift". **The ratchet cannot see that direction.** Measured, before any pin for the twin existed: with the zod key declared and `cardTitle?: string` deleted from the interface, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` exited **0** — including its third leg `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, which is the leg that judges the ratchet.

Filed as **objectui#9711** and re-derived there from the ratchet's source. ⚠️ The conclusion holds and the first cut of this PR got the **mechanism** wrong; it is corrected here and in the code, because the corrected one is sharper. The three operators are blind for three *different* reasons:

- `WiderThanDeclaredKeys` maps over `MirroredKeys` intersected with `DeclaredKeys`, so a key the twin does not declare simply **leaves the key set** — blind by omission.
- `NarrowerThanDeclared` maps over `MirroredKeys` intersected with `keyof D` — `keyof D`, not `DeclaredKeys` — and `keyof D` is absorbed by `BaseSchema`'s `[key: string]: any`, so the compared type is `any` and every mirror fits it. This is the **only** operator the index signature explains.
- `UnmirroredDeclaredKeys` measures the opposite subtraction, declared-but-unmirrored.

⛔ So `DeclaredKeys` does **not** read the twin as accepting every name — `WithoutIndexSignature` exists precisely to strip index signatures, and the first cut of this section said otherwise. The sharpest framing is the file's own history: it already closed this failure mode **by name** for one direction (objectui#6058 measured it; `UnmirroredDeclaredKeys` was added to close it) and there is no counterpart operator for mirrored-but-undeclared. One direction closed by name, its reverse left open.

The twin is still right, and the ruling's **instruction** stands — it is the published `.d.ts` surface an author's editor reads, and with the member declared TypeScript refuses `cardTitle: 42` in a typed corpus where the index signature alone would admit it. What does not stand is the ratchet as its guarantor. Rather than ship a declaration no instrument can defend, this PR gives it one: a `@ts-expect-error` row on `cardTitle: 42` in the pin file, whose directive goes unused — TS2578 — the moment the member is deleted. Leg 2 below is that instrument being measured both ways.

### The rationale correction (commit `d4ba7e370`)

The first cut published the disproved guarantee in **five** places this branch adds, one of them the changeset body — which publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG, so the release note would have shipped the guarantee as fact. All five now state what holds and nothing more:

| # | where | now says |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.changeset/9606-object-kanban-card-title.md` | the two faces accept and refuse the same documents; the agreement is held by this change's own pin, not by the ratchet, with objectui#9711 cited |
| 2 | the `cardTitle?: string` docblock in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` | same, plus what the member buys against the index signature |
| 3 | the comment above `cardTitle:` in `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` | same |
| 4 | the pin file's mechanism paragraph | the corrected three-operator reading above |
| 5 | the `NEITHER_SPELLING_BOARD` docblock in the pin file | "both members are OPTIONAL on both faces, so the two faces agree on this board too" |

Rows 4 and 5 are beyond the three the reviewer's `git grep` found — they carry the same disproved claim under different wording, in files this PR adds, so leaving them would have shipped it anyway.

⚠️ **Two pre-existing pending changesets, not one, publish that same sentence** — `.changeset/5903-objectgantt-declared-keys.md` and `.changeset/6051-gantt-flat-config-declared-keys.md`. A line-based `git grep` finds only 6051; 5903 wraps the sentence across two lines, so the count needs a whitespace-insensitive scan. ⛔ Neither is touched here — neither is this PR's, and objectui#9711 is where the class belongs.

Every exit code above was captured to disk before any pipe.

## `changeset-claim-re-read` — the verdict the gate asks for

The gate re-ran on this branch and listed **22** pending changesets naming `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` or `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`. It exits 0, blocks nothing and judges name resolution rather than meaning; the reading below is the meaning half.

**Verdict: no claim among the 22 goes false.** The premise, verified on the current head rather than inherited: this diff is purely **additive** — `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD` reads `+341 / -0` across four files, zero deletions — and it adds exactly one optional key to one schema. So a claim can only go false if it asserts `cardTitle` is undeclared on `ObjectKanbanSchema`, or gives an exhaustive key list for that schema that is now incomplete. Read at paragraph level, not line level. Four of the 22 carry kanban or card-title content and were read in full:

- **`7322-object-kanban-group-by-limit.md`** — about `groupField` / `groupBy` / `limit`. Its key statements are scoped to those three; its general one ("`BaseSchema`'s unknown-key policy is byte-identical, an undeclared key still passes through") is untouched. Holds.
- **`8990-object-kanban-groupby-optional.md`** — about `groupBy` requiredness and what a lane-less board does. Names no other key of the arm. Holds.
- **`8913-object-kanban-columns-declared.md`** — about `columns`. Its "declaring here can only narrow, the value was already `any`" reasoning is the same class as this change and stays true. Holds.
- **`7804-objectql-handler-key-arms.md`** — `titleField` appears only as a **lit control string** in a grep census, not as a claim about a declaration. Holds.

The remaining 18 name the two files for chart, form-section, grid, tree, alert-dialog, drill-down, barrel-export, docblock and line-citation reasons with no `object-kanban` arm claim in the paragraph.

### ⚠️ Volunteered beyond the gate's set — two claims that DO move, neither of them mine

Both are outside the 22 because neither names the two files in backticks, so the gate never asked about them. I read them because this worktree was the cheapest place to answer, and I am **not** editing them:

- **`.changeset/8802-8257-8008-kanban-gantt-family-retirement.md`** — the sharpest one. Present tense: "That arm was the only schema face that ever declared `columns`, `cardTitle`, `swimlaneField`, `grouping` and `navigation` … **The surviving `ObjectKanbanSchema` face declares none of them.**" That sentence is false for `cardTitle` after this PR. ⭐ It was **already** false for `columns` — objectui#8913 declared `columns` on this same arm and did not correct it — so the precedent for this exact class is "left uncorrected", and this PR is the second instance rather than the first. The same paragraph also says declaring these keys on `ObjectKanbanSchema` "would WIDEN a published accept set, which is a maintainer ruling and not part of this one", which is precisely the ruling that authorised this card.
- **`.changeset/7322-object-kanban-component-props.md`** — its read-set census lists "`columns`, `cardTitle`, `swimlaneField`, `grouping` — `KanbanSchema` only". Already stale twice over before this PR (`columns` via objectui#8913, and `KanbanSchema` itself retired by objectui#8802), and this change adds `cardTitle` as a third. ⚠️ Not the `:47` line, which says "`cardTitle` (already declared)" about `KanbanSchema` and is **not** a contradiction — the claim that moves is the census bullet.

Whether either body is corrected is the PM's to route: they are other cards' declarations, the gate did not raise them, and the correction the gate documents ("correct the body, prose-only, frontmatter untouched") is a write on someone else's pending release note.

## Acceptance notes — found, deliberately not done

- **`ObjectKanban.tsx`'s docblock above `KanbanTitleFieldSource` is now stale.** It says the structural interface exists because "neither declares both keys — `KanbanSchema` declares `cardTitle` and tombstones `titleField`, `ObjectKanbanSchema` declares `titleField` and reaches `cardTitle` through `BaseSchema`'s index signature". After this PR the `object-kanban` arm declares **both**. The sentence, not the code, is what goes wrong. Not repaired here: it lives in `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`, outside this card's declared file surface and outside the package this contract review is at tier for, and touching it would pull that package's whole test surface and a second package's release accounting into a one-line contract change. Noted, not filed — the carrier is the next PR that edits `resolveKanbanTitleField` or its precedence pins.
- **The mirror's `titleField` describe still reads `'Title field'`,** not the spec's "Legacy fallback for `cardTitle` … Prefer `cardTitle`". Carrying that text over would be an improvement and it is exactly what the ruling told this card not to do — "do not touch it beyond leaving it declared". Noted, not filed; it belongs to whatever card eventually converts the alias.
- **The zod-mirror-parity ratchet's blind direction** (the section above) is a real property of a live guard, measured with a control. It is not filed from here because filing is the triage seat's, and it is reported to the PM with dedupe words instead: `zod-mirror-parity` · mirrored-but-undeclared · `WithoutIndexSignature` · `BaseSchema` index signature · ratchet blind direction.
